answer: Each agent identity is anchored to a verifiable-delay puzzle: before its first trade, the agent must complete a slow, non-parallelizable computation whose elapsed time is measured against a quartz-stabilized clock, producing a unique timing proof. Forging one identity costs minutes of real time; forging ten thousand costs months. Peers then echo the proof: every attestation references the timing certificate, so duplicates sharing one clock signature cluster together and are rejected. The honest cost is one short wait; the attacker's cost is time itself.
